R116.summary: A copy of Philip II's letter to the nuncio with two cipher passages. A: on urging the Emperor his brother to join the new league proposed by the Pope, Philip is sending a special envoy and has ordered fitting representations; His Holiness should do the same. B: he has seen the separate sheet on the affairs of Pitigliano and desires the peace of all Italy, and will do all he can to remove any occasion that might disturb it. Context: Gregory XIII's league against the Turks, which collapsed when Venice made peace in 1573.
R116.en:
Passage A (f. 303r). As to making representations to the Emperor my brother [?so that] he [?enter] the new league
proposed by His Holiness: I am sending a special envoy [?to] treat of this business, and I have ordered that on this
[?particular] those good representations be made that seemed fitting to me; and although on my [?side] I have had
[…] of the good […], nevertheless on my part all the good representations will go on being made to the Emperor that
are understood [?to be] most to the purpose, as in a business that is of such service to God and so desired by
[?all] [?Italy]. It will be [?well] that His Holiness [?also] do the same on his side, as you say he offers.

Passage B (f. 304r). I have seen the sheet sent to me separately on the affairs of Pitigliano, and understood
[?in detail] all that has happened, and what His Holiness [?wishes] to be done on my part.

snip.cap: R116, f. 303r: the end of the clear copy of Philip II’s letter and the first lines of cipher passage A

system: Homophonic substitution on digit signs (two per letter, dotted and undotted, zero rule), a stroke on 2/4/5 as word end, a small nomenclator, no doubled letters, final nulls: the Spain nunciature's 'cifra ordinaria'.
